entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9080"/><div sID="gen15343" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9080"/><hi type="bold">2. Who--</hi>else but God? The fact that God "raiseth up" Cyrus and qualifies him for becoming the conqueror of the nations and deliverer of God's people, is a strong argument why they should trust in Him. The future is here prophetically represented as present or past.<div eID="gen15343" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15344" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the righteous man--</hi>Cyrus; as <reference osisRef="Isa.44.28">Is 44:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.45.1-Isa.45.4">45:1-4</reference>, 13; 46:11, "from the East," prove. Called "righteous," not so much on account of his own equity [Herodotus, 3.89], as because he fulfilled God's righteous will in restoring the Jews from their unjust captivity. Raised him up in righteousness. The Septuagint takes the Hebrew as a noun "righteousness." Maurer translates, "Who raised up him whom salvation (national and temporal, the gift of God's 'righteousness' to the good, <reference osisRef="Isa.32.17">Is 32:17</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Isa.45.8">Is 45:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.51.5">51:5</reference>) meets at his foot" (that is, wherever he goes). Cyrus is said to come from the East, because Persia is east of Babylon; but in <reference osisRef="Isa.41.25">Is 41:25</reference>, from the north, in reference to Media. At the same time the full sense of righteousness, or righteous, and of the whole passage, is realized only in Messiah, Cyrus' antitype (Cyrus knew not God, <reference osisRef="Isa.45.4">Is 45:4</reference>). He goes forth as the Universal Conqueror of the "nations," in righteousness making war (<reference osisRef="Ps.2.8">Psa 2:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.9">9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.19.11-Rev.15.6">Re 19:11-15; 6</reference>:2; 2:26, 27). "The idols He shall utterly abolish" (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.7.23">Is 7:23</reference>, with <reference osisRef="Isa.2.18">Is 2:18</reference>). Righteousness was always raised up from the East. Paradise was east of Eden. The cherubim were at the east of the garden. Abraham was called from the East. Judea, the birthplace of Messiah, was in the East.<div eID="gen15344" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15345" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">called ... to ... foot--</hi>called him to attend His (God's) steps, that is, follow His guidance. In <reference osisRef="Ezra.1.2">Ezr 1:2</reference>, Cyrus acknowledges Jehovah as the Giver of his victories. He subdued the nations from the Euxine to the Red Sea, and even Egypt (says Xenophon).<div eID="gen15345" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15346" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">dust--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.17.13">Is 17:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.29.5">29:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.18.42">Psa 18:42</reference>). Persia, Cyrus' country, was famed for the use of the "bow" (<reference osisRef="Isa.22.6">Is 22:6</reference>). "Before him" means "gave them into his power" (<reference osisRef="Josh.10.12">Jos 10:12</reference>). Maurer translates, "Gave his (the enemy's) sword to be dust, and his (the enemy's) bow to be as stubble" (<reference osisRef="Job.41.26">Job 41:26</reference>, <reference osisRef="Job.41.29">29</reference>). <div eID="gen15346" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9100"/><div sID="gen15391" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9100"/><hi type="bold">22. what shall happen--</hi>"Let them bring near and declare future contingencies" [Horsley].<div eID="gen15391" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15392" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">former things ... the latter end of them--</hi>show what former predictions the idols have given, that we may compare the event ("latter end") with them; or give new prophecies ("declare things to come") (<reference osisRef="Isa.42.9">Is 42:9</reference>), [Maurer]. Barnes explains it more reconditely, "Let them foretell the entire series of events, showing, in their order, the things which shall first occur, as well as those which shall finally happen"; the false prophets tried to predict isolated events, having no mutual dependency; not a long series of events mutually and orderly connected, and stretching far into futurity. They did not even try to do this. None but God can do it (<reference osisRef="Isa.46.10">Is 46:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.44.7">44:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.44.8">8</reference>). "Or ... things to come" will, in this view, mean, Let them, if they cannot predict the series, even predict plainly any detached events. <div eID="gen15392" type="x-p"/>
